Category C; use only if benefit justifies risk
Excretion in milk unknown; use caution, avoid breast application

summary: Adapalene is a topical retinoid for acne vulgaris that normalizes follicular keratinization and has anti-inflammatory and comedolytic effects. Applied as a thin layer once daily (0.1% available OTC, 0.3% by prescription). Local irritation - erythema, dryness, scaling, burning - is common early; sun protection is advised. Systemic absorption is minimal.
indications: Topical treatment of acne vulgaris in patients 12 years of age and older

dosage.d: Thin layer of 0.1% gel/cream/lotion to affected area once daily at bedtime
dosage.n: OTC strength; cleanse and pat dry first

dosage.d: Thin layer of 0.3% gel once daily

admin: Cleanse the area with a mild or soapless cleanser and pat dry before applying
Apply a thin layer over the entire affected area, not just individual lesions
Avoid eyes, lips, mucous membranes, and cuts/abrasions/eczematous skin
Do not apply more than once daily; more does not work faster and increases irritation
Use a moisturizer and sunscreen; expect therapeutic effect over 8-12 weeks
moa: Adapalene binds to specific retinoic acid nuclear receptors (RAR), modulating cellular differentiation, keratinization and inflammatory processes within the follicle. This normalizes desquamation of follicular epithelium, reduces microcomedone formation, and exerts anti-inflammatory activity, improving acne.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to adapalene or formulation components
relative: Eczema or seborrheic dermatitis on treatment area

preg: Pregnancy Category C. No well-controlled trials in pregnant women; oral animal doses far above topical exposure were teratogenic. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. Systemic absorption from topical use is very low.
lact: It is not known whether adapalene is excreted in human milk. Exercise caution when used in a nursing woman and avoid application to the breast/chest area to prevent infant exposure.
renal: Systemic absorption is negligible; no renal dose adjustment needed.
hepatic: Systemic absorption is negligible; no hepatic dose adjustment needed.

moderate: Other topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide, salicylic acid, sulfur, resorcinol - additive skin irritation/drying
Topical products with high alcohol, astringents, spices or lime - increased irritation
minor: Abrasive cleansers, medicated soaps, harsh scrubs - cumulative irritation
interactions.alcohol: No systemic interaction; avoid alcohol-containing skin products that worsen dryness.

serious: Severe irritant or allergic contact dermatitis
emergency: Severe allergic reaction (swelling, hives, difficulty breathing)

monitoring: Local tolerance: erythema, dryness, scaling, stinging - reduce frequency if excessive
counsel: Apply a thin layer once daily, usually at night, to the whole affected area after cleansing
Some redness, dryness and peeling are expected early and usually lessen with continued use
Use a non-comedogenic moisturizer and daily sunscreen; limit sun and sunlamp exposure
Avoid eyes, lips and mucous membranes; do not wax treated skin
Be patient - visible improvement may take 8-12 weeks; do not over-apply
pk: Minimal systemic exposure; not clinically relevant
Store at controlled room temperature; avoid freezing
pearls: 0.1% adapalene gel is available OTC; 0.3% gel is prescription for more resistant acne
Better photostability and tolerability than older retinoids (tretinoin)
Often combined with benzoyl peroxide for synergistic effect
Apply to the whole acne-prone area, not just spots - it is preventive (comedolytic)
Counsel on expected initial irritation to support adherence
missed: If a once-daily application is missed, apply it when remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose; do not apply extra to make up. Resume the regular once-daily schedule.
overdose: Topical overuse causes increased local irritation (erythema, peeling, discomfort) rather than systemic toxicity. Discontinue or reduce frequency and treat the skin with bland emollients. Ingestion should be managed with standard supportive care.
